newsitem.title: UK: Redwood bids for UK Conservative leadership.
newsitem.headline: Redwood bids for UK Conservative leadership.

text.p: Rightwinger John Redwood has said he will stand as a candidate for leadership of the Conservative Party.
"I can't defend the past, I can unite the party," he wrote in the Tuesday edition of the London Times.

"In sadness at the size of our defeat, in humility at the verdict of the people, but with optimism for the future, I put myself forward for the leadership," said Redwood who unsucessfully challenged John Major in a 1995 leadership contest.

Kenneth Clarke, the pro-European finance minister, has already thrown his hat into the ring along with right-winger Peter Lilley. Former interior minister Michael Howard is also expected to join the field.
Major announced he was to step down after the Conservatives suffered their worst election defeat in more than 150 years. Labour's Tony Blair won a landslide victory on May Day.
